items.title: Master Shipwright Builds a Boat He Designed Himself | Start to Finish by @TipsfromaShipwright
items.description: Master shipwright Louis Sauzedde spent years waiting for the right moment to bring one of his own boat designs to life. When that moment finally came, he began turning raw lumber into a traditional wooden skiff — combining generations of boatbuilding knowledge with clever modern techniques. From vacuum-laminating the white oak transom and shaping the hull by hand to building a layered V-bottom reinforced with fiberglass, almost every stage reveals a different solution to a difficult problem. Along the way, Louis relies on carefully selected timber, laminated structural parts, custom fittings, and small tricks learned through decades of working with wood. items.title: Couple Builds a Greenhouse With a Giant Underground Heat Battery | Start to Finish by @thetielife
items.description: Minus thirty-two degrees. That's what this greenhouse has to survive. In British Columbia, winter shuts a garden down for months. The ground freezes for weeks at a time. James and Michelle built a 1,300 square foot greenhouse designed to keep producing food straight through it — and almost none of what makes it work is visible. Hundreds of feet of pipe are buried in the soil beneath the floor. When the greenhouse overheats, warm air gets pushed down into that network and the ground absorbs it. When it cools, the same ground gives it back. The walls are rammed earth, packed twelve feet high into forms that had to hold under enormous pressure. The roof is carried by a single tamarack trunk, charred black with fire. Then, on the same property, they built a sauna — out of the same earth, with students who came to learn how. The Tie Life Homestead https://www.youtube.com/@thetielife https://www.thetielife.com/ https://www.instagram.com/the_tie_life/ 00:00 A Greenhouse Built for Minus Thirty-Two 02:35 Building the Formwork 03:35 Mixing the Earth 07:31 Racing the Deep Freeze 09:57 The Climate Battery 12:00 A Tamarack Trunk as the Center Post 13:00 Raising the Roof 17:16 Closing In the Greenhouse 18:05 Building the Sauna 20:45 What They're Really Building

items.title: Veteran Family Builds an Arch Cabin on 10 Acres | Start to Finish by @chasingfreedomhomestead
items.description: Almost every building material starts out straight. This cabin doesn't have a single straight wall. After 32 years in the military and 8 more in law enforcement, Matt bought 10 acres in the Pacific Northwest with his wife Brenda and their son Isaac. The first structure going up is an arch cabin — 22 curved steel ribs forming one continuous shell from the ground on one side to the ground on the other. Nothing about it is standard. OSB comes square and has to be cut to the curve. A 2,500-gallon water tank goes into the crawl space before the floor does, because afterward it won't fit. A pony wall runs around the entire base — 38 separate pieces — just to keep the wiring away from hot metal. The property had a house before. It burned down. This is what goes there now. items.title: Couple Builds a 4,000 Sq Ft Home From 6 Shipping Containers | Start to Finish by @sunfishbudget
items.description: One winter in Minnesota, Ian walked into a shipping container to pick up a part. It was freezing outside, but inside, a single fan heater kept the whole box warm. That was the idea. Nine years later, he and Janna sold their home, bought sixty acres next door, tore down the hundred-year-old farmhouse on it, and built a 4,000 square foot house out of six shipping containers. Fourteen steel columns. Nine massive beams. Containers cut down until one lost its entire floor. Three-inch white oak planks laid straight onto the steel. And a tile they tore out and replaced after it was already installed, because under all that natural light it read blue instead of gray. Sunfish Budget https://www.youtube.com/@SunfishBudget https://www.sunfishbudget.com/ https://www.instagram.com/sunfish.budget 00:00 Six Containers and Nine Years 01:30 Precision Starts at the Foundation 03:35 Cutting the Containers Apart 04:30 Standing the Steel Columns 06:23 Racing the Minnesota Winter 09:55 Spray Foam in the Cold 11:30 Lifting the Massive Windows 13:08 Designing Around the Containers 14:03 The Siding Problem 18:22 The Custom Staircase 24:32 The Tile They Tore Out

items.title: Couple Builds a Massive Concrete Duplex in the Desert | Start to Finish by @Handeeman
items.description: Most houses start with a wooden frame. This one doesn't. In the Arizona desert, Derek and Hanna built their home from ICF — foam blocks stacked into walls, then filled with concrete. The foam stays. The concrete becomes the structure. Steel fibers mixed straight into the slab instead of rebar. A polished concrete floor that was decided months before anyone saw it. A gray-water system that puts shower water back into the landscape. A steel patio fabricated on site. A staircase that glows from underneath. items.title: Man Spends Years Rebuilding an Abandoned Stone House in the Forest Alone | by @luxonbushcraft​
items.description: Twenty years ago, Martin decided he wanted a different kind of life — quieter, simpler, closer to nature. Years later he found an abandoned stone house, built in 1957 and forgotten in the forest for decades. Most people would have walked away. This is the full story of what happened next: a new roof, stone walls repaired one by one, insulation, a handmade front door, a wood stove, solar panels, a covered terrace built from massive natural timber, an outdoor kitchen, and a garden — almost all of it built alone, with his dog Laika beside him. In this video Martin also tells the story himself: why he chose a ruin, when he almost gave up, and what viewers never see behind the finished footage. In this full build documentary, a civil engineer with real-world construction experience takes on one of the most ambitious residential projects imaginable. Built on challenging mountainous terrain, this A-Frame house features panoramic mountain views, floor-to-ceiling glazing, a traditional brick fireplace, radiant floor heating, a designer circular swimming pool, and a breathtaking glass-enclosed living space that brings the outdoors in. Every phase of construction is captured — from the reinforced concrete foundation and massive timber A-frame structure, to the pool tiling, interior finishing, landscaping, and final furnishing. Every beam, plank, and connection is carefully crafted by skilled builders using traditional techniques that have stood the test of time.
